reading.body:
CyrusOne Sterling (NVA9) is a 38 MW, 700,000-square-foot data center that ranks 13th among Virginia's 25 facilities with published capacity, representing 2.4 percent of the state's disclosed IT load.

The 25 facilities with published figures total 1,603 MW, so Sterling sits at the median of disclosed capacity rather than among the largest campuses. At a typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, its 38 MW would support roughly 950 racks, but that is an assumption about possible scale, not a stated configuration. The facility publishes no certifications, so its qualification to host any particular workload class, including high-density AI training, is not stated.

Virginia has 330 mapped data center facilities overall, and the vast majority publish no capacity number. Sterling's position therefore reflects only the small disclosed subset, not the state's full IT load. The data does not state grid capacity, local grid ability to absorb new load, or any announced expansion, so it cannot show whether this facility is constrained by power or positioned for growth.
